subject: english-studies
title: Comparing with adjectives
summary: Use tall, taller and tallest, and good, better and best, correctly.

lesson.text: An adjective describes a noun: a tall tree, a sweet mango. When we compare things, the adjective changes form.

items: Comparative (two things): Ola is taller than Femi.
Superlative (three or more): Ola is the tallest in the class.
big → bigger → biggest (double the last letter)

lesson.title: Fill the gap: Lagos is ___ than Ibadan. (busy)
steps: Two places are compared, so use the comparative.
Busy ends in a consonant + y: busy → busier.

lesson.text: Never use both: "more bigger" and "most tallest" are wrong. Use either -er/-est or more/most, not both.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: This mango is ___ than that one.
questions.explanation: Two mangoes are compared, so use the comparative: sweeter. "More sweeter" uses both forms, which is wrong.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: Zainab is the ___ runner in the school.
questions.explanation: She is compared with everyone in the school (more than two), so use the superlative: fastest.
Good is irregular: good → better → best. "Gooder" is not a word.

options: This is the most cheapest shop.
My bag is more heavy than yours.
Kano is more bigger than Jos.
This is the most beautiful dress.
questions.explanation: Beautiful is long, so it takes most. The others should be cheapest, heavier and bigger.
Bad is irregular: bad → worse → worst. Worse is the comparative, for two things.
